title: "Predictive modeling of claims status"
author: 'Lucy Cao, Kaitlyn Chihaoui, Alex Dieter, Srinidhi Sathish, Emily Tian'
date: today

### Abstract
We used the cleaned text scraped from the webpages—combining both paragraph content and header tags—and converted it into TF–IDF features for predictive modeling. For the binary classification task, regularized logistic regression (ridge) achieved the highest accuracy (77.18%), outperforming both the support vector machine and the recurrent neural network. For the multiclass task, an LSTM-based recurrent neural network performed best, reaching 60.26% accuracy, compared to 46.41% for ridge logistic regression and 44.87% for the SVM. These two models were selected as our final binary and multiclass classifiers, respectively, and were exported along with their corresponding test-set predictions.



### Preprocessing

We scraped and combined both paragraph text and HTML header tags from each webpage. All text was lowercased and cleaned by removing punctuation, numbers, URLs, email addresses, and extra whitespace. CamelCase splitting, tokenization, lemmatization, and stop-word removal were performed to normalize textual content. The resulting tokens were converted into TF–IDF–weighted document–term matrices, which served as the input features for all downstream models. Feature names were saved separately to ensure consistent column ordering when applying the models to the test dataset.


### Methods
### Binary Classification

We evaluated three models for the binary claim vs. non-claim prediction task: a Support Vector Machine (RBF kernel), regularized logistic regression (ridge), and a recurrent neural network (LSTM).

**Support Vector Machine (RBF):**  
Used TF–IDF features with an RBF kernel. Hyperparameters were tuned over a limited grid to balance model flexibility and computational cost.

**Regularized Logistic Regression (Ridge):**  
Applied a ridge penalty with the tuning parameter λ selected by cross-validation. This model fits a linear decision boundary in the high-dimensional sparse TF–IDF feature space.

**Recurrent Neural Network (LSTM):**  
Constructed with an embedding layer, an LSTM layer, and dropout regularization. Due to package-loading issues encountered when reloading the model, we were only able to compute **accuracy** for this model.  
*Professor Coburn confirmed that reporting accuracy alone is acceptable for this deliverable.*


Across these models, **ridge logistic regression achieved the highest accuracy** and was therefore selected as the final binary classifier.

#### Multiclass classification

For the multiclass task, we evaluated Support Vector Machine (RBF kernel), regularized logistic regression (ridge), and an LSTM-based recurrent neural network.

**Support Vector Machine (RBF):**  
Implemented using a one-vs-rest extension of the binary RBF SVM applied to TF–IDF features.

**Regularized Logistic Regression (Ridge):**  
Extended to the multiclass setting with a one-vs-rest formulation and ridge regularization.

**Recurrent Neural Network (LSTM):**  
Built with an embedding layer, LSTM layer, and dropout regularization, and trained with categorical cross-entropy using the Adam optimizer. Due to library-loading issues encountered when reloading the model for evaluation, we were only able to compute **accuracy** for this model.  
*Professor Coburn confirmed that reporting accuracy alone is acceptable for this deliverable.*


Among all models, the **LSTM-based RNN achieved the highest accuracy (0.6026)** and was selected as the final multiclass classifier. The model was exported in `.keras` format for deployment.


### Results 
#### Binary classification metrics

| Model                         | Accuracy | Sensitivity | Specificity |
|-------------------------------|----------|-------------|-------------|
| Support Vector Machine (RBF)  | 0.6154   | 0.378 | 0.8895 |
| Regularized Logistic (Ridge)  | **0.7718** | 0.7656 | 0.779 |
| Recurrent Neural Network (RNN)| 0.5385   | — | —  |

Final model: Ridge logistic regression.
---

#### Multiclass classification metrics

| Model                         | Accuracy | Sensitivity (macro) | Specificity (macro) |
|-------------------------------|----------|----------------------|----------------------|
| Support Vector Machine (RBF)  | 0.4487   | 0.1934       | 0.7982       |
| Regularized Logistic (Ridge)  | 0.4641   | 0.2         | 0.8        |
| Recurrent Neural Network (RNN)| **0.6026** |  —   |   —   |

Final model: Multiclass LSTM-based RNN.
